chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Attar from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj from Yunus from Abu Wahb al-Qasri, who said:

I entered the city and went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I came to you but had not yet visited the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Bad is what you did, if it were not that you are from our Shias, I would not have looked at you. Do you not visit he whom Allah the Almighty visits with the angels, and the Prophets (peace be upon them) visit, and the believers visit?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I did not know that.' He said, 'Then know that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) is with Allah superior to all the Imams, and he has the reward of their deeds, and they are favored according to the measure of his deeds.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the grave of Imam Ali (AS) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the theological centrality of Imam Ali (AS) within Shia tradition, portraying his grave as a focal point of divine and prophetic visitation. The Imam’s statement that the rewards of all subsequent Imams are derived from Ali’s status highlights the concept of *Fadilat al-Aimmah* (superiority of the Imams), establishing Ali as the foundational source of spiritual merit for the entire lineage of Imams.
